Quick answers:
- MVP activation checklist: see tab "MVP" in redwood-mvp-activation-checklist.xlsx. It includes prerequisites (VPC peering/KMS), acceptance tests, and a go/no-go signoff table.
- Procurement path: reserved capacity is reserved via a Commitment Agreement (monthly or annual). We accept PO + net30; for annual commits we provide a billing credit schedule. I added a summary page for Finance.
- Region mapping: recommend primary pool in us-west (lower median latency to your control plane) with us-east as warm standby for failover. Rough token-latency delta estimated at 6-12ms for typical gen workloads.

Action items I propose this week:
- Ben: I'll need a short procurement one-pager for your Finance team (Ben, can you draft and send by Monday?).
- Irene: can you scope the autoscale guardrails and burst-credit policy we should recommend for a 2x burst profile?
- Asha/Marco: please confirm whether a single shared pool (multi-tenant dedicated) is acceptable or if you require VPC-isolated nodes for data controls.

I'll schedule a 30-min alignment with Procurement and NetOps after Ben's one-pager lands.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Adding the procurement one-pager here (summary below) — full doc is attached.

Summary for Procurement (one-pager):
- Commercial model: Reserved capacity commitment available monthly or annual. Annual gives 10% effective discount and predictable unit economics.
- Billing: Net30 invoices. We issue an initial invoice for the committed minimum at activation then monthly invoices thereafter.
- PO and SOW: PO to Finance + signed Commitment Agreement to Legal. Typical SOW includes pool size, region(s), and autoscale/burst policy parameters.
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for reserved pools; regional failover documented in the SOW.

Requests for NovaVision:
- Confirm desired commitment term (monthly / 12-month) by Tue, Dec 7.
- Confirm if you need VPC-isolated nodes.

I'll be on the procurement call Tuesday to walk through invoicing and payment options.

Ben Carter

Asha/Team — outlining recommended autoscale & burst guardrails for the MVP: 

Autoscale baseline:
- Min pool: 4x A100-equivalents (warm capacity for steady-state traffic).
- Target scale: up to 12x for typical peak patterns (3x baseline).
- Scale-up policy: 60s sustained CPU/GPU utilization >75% or queue length threshold >120 requests.
- Scale-down: gradual over 10m to avoid oscillation.

Burst credits:
- We recommend a burst budget equivalent to 2x baseline for short windows (credits consumed over 24h).
- Soft fallback: if burst credits depleted, route to cheaper quantized model variant with 15-30% slower throughput but preserved correctness.

Operational handoffs:
- NetOps tasks: VPC peering, required IP ranges, and test-traffic endpoints (I will send an ops checklist).
- CS checklist: run acceptance tests in the checklist tab; CS and NV engineer to sign off before activation.

I'll attach a short netops checklist in follow-up. If you need tighter latency SLOs we can discuss adding geo-replicated pools, but that will change cost profiles.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
